If your Phoenix couch-disposal knowledge dates to a few years ago, it's obsolete: the city **retired the old quarterly bulk-trash routes** — where crews drove every street four times a year looking for piles — and replaced them with an **appointment system**. The change is genuinely better for residents who know about it: you pick the date instead of waiting for your area's quarter. It's worse for the ones who don't, because the old habit of dragging a couch to the curb "for bulk week" is now an early-placement citation.

## The Appointment System, Exactly

- **Schedule online or by phone:** phoenix.gov/publicworks/bulktrash or 602-262-6251.
- **Book at least three business days ahead;** appointments open up to four weeks out.
- **Four collections per household per calendar year** — furniture, appliances, and yard debris all qualify.
- **Placement window:** items go to the curb **no more than seven days before your appointment date**, and only after the appointment exists. Phoenix enforces early placement; a couch at the curb with no appointment attached is how citations happen.
- Regular trash rules still apply to anything bin-sized — bulk appointments are for what genuinely can't fit the container.

The strategic wrinkle: four pickups a year is a budget. Spending one appointment on a single couch in January means three left for the rest of the year's projects — worth a thought before booking the city for one item.

## The Other Phoenix Routes

**Transfer stations** accept resident drop-offs if you have a truck and would rather not spend an appointment. **Donation** deserves first consideration in a city with year-round moving season — a couch that [passes condition standards](/blog/eco-friendly-living/can-couch-be-donated/) can be picked up by charity programs instead of landfilled. And one Phoenix-specific warning from physics: desert sun destroys upholstery fast — a couch "waiting at the curb for a while" in July comes back unfit for donation in days, not weeks.

**When the appointment math doesn't work** — you're out of annual pickups, the three-day lead time collides with a move, or the couch is up a flight of stairs: [couch removal in Phoenix](/az/phoenix/couch-removal/) starts at $90, carry-out included, [same-day in most ZIPs before 2PM EST](/book-online/), with [donation routing](/az/phoenix/donation-pickup/) first for anything in good shape. Item pricing is in the [cost guide](/blog/junk-removal/how-much-does-couch-removal-cost/).

## Frequently Asked Questions

### Does Phoenix still do quarterly bulk trash pickup?

No — the quarterly route system was replaced with scheduled appointments. Residents now book a specific date (up to four per year) instead of waiting for their area's quarterly sweep.

### How do I schedule a bulk trash pickup in Phoenix?

At phoenix.gov/publicworks/bulktrash or by calling 602-262-6251, at least three business days in advance. Appointments can be booked up to four weeks ahead.

### When can I put my couch at the curb in Phoenix?

Only after you have an appointment, and no more than seven days before it. Early placement without a scheduled date is a citable offense — the rule the appointment system enforces hardest.

### What's the fastest way to remove a couch in Phoenix?

Booked removal beats the three-business-day municipal lead time: [same-day across most of Phoenix](/az/phoenix/couch-removal/) when booked before 2PM EST, with the carry from inside your home included.
